metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent attempted to change text colors of three textboxes on slide 1. Failed at step 9 when it selected wrong colors from the palette (Gold, Dark Gray 4 instead of pure yellow).
metadata.capability_extraction: Can click textboxes, select text (Ctrl+A), open Format > Character > Font Effects, use color picker dropdown
metadata.failure_analysis: Model failed specifically when picking yellow from the color palette — selected 'Gold' (darker orange-yellow) first, then 'Dark Gray 4'. Demonstrates difficulty with precise color palette selection.
metadata.task_rationale: This isolates the very first sub-goal from the trajectory: change NEW PRODUCT to yellow. This was the first action the agent attempted before the deviation point (step 9).
metadata.explanation: Task requires changing only the NEW PRODUCT textbox color to pure yellow (FFFF00). Evaluator reads PPTX after save and checks font color of text containing 'NEW PR'. Initial state F8E6DA fails yellow check.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly targets the right file (/home/user/Desktop/45_2.pptx), slide (index 0 = slide 1), and text shape containing 'NEW PR' (partial match for 'NEW PRODUCT') — semantically correct.

Metric correctly handles expected.type='rule': accesses expected.get('expected_color') and expected.get('tolerance') directly on the rules dict, which is what the framework passes when type='rule'. No incorrect patterns like expected.get('rules', {}).
Expected color FFFF00 (pure yellow, RGB 255,255,0) matches the instruction requirement ('change to yellow'). Tolerance of 10 per channel is appropriately strict.
Postconfig saves the file with Ctrl+S before verification — necessary and correct for file-based PPTX getter.
Negative control resistance is good: initial state color F8E6DA (248,230,218) is far from yellow (255,255,0) and would correctly fail the check.
Single-requirement task (one color change) is fully covered by the single getter+metric pair.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: The getter returns only the FIRST run with an explicit color in the matching shape. If the 'NEW PRODUCT' text consists of multiple runs and only some runs are changed to yellow, the getter could return a false positive. Consider iterating all runs and returning the majority or last color, or verifying all runs are yellow. In practice this is unlikely to cause issues since LibreOffice applies color to all selected text uniformly.
